commit.message:
[SPARK-59696][SQL] Skip the redundant second modulo in integral MathUtils.pmod for positive divisors

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

For integral `MathUtils.pmod(a, n)` with `n > 0`, skip the redundant second modulo in the released `r = a % n; if (r < 0) (r + n) % n else r`. For `n > 0` the result is `Math.floorMod(a, n)`: a negative remainder only needs `n` added. This PR computes it with a branchless sign fix-up:

```scala
def pmod(a: Int, n: Int): Int = {
  val r = a % n
  if (n > 0) r + (n & (r >> 31)) else if (r >= 0) r else (r + n) % n
}
// Long: the same with `r >> 63`.
```

`n < 0` keeps the original `(r + n) % n`. `Byte`/`Short` delegate to `Int`. `Float`/`Double` are unchanged.

### Why are the changes needed?

`pmod` with a positive divisor is the common case (e.g. `HashPartitioning` passes `numPartitions` for every row), and the second `% n` is a no-op there.

The fix-up is written out because `Math.floorMod` adjusts with a data-dependent conditional, which C2 often keeps as a branch that mispredicts on random-sign dividends. JMH 1.37, x86_64, 16,384 `pmod(int, int)` calls per op over random-sign dividends, 3 forks x 10 iterations; us/op:

| divisor | JDK | released | `Math.floorMod` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JIT constant `200` | 17 | 20.5 | 31.9 (bimodal) | 14.9 |
| | 25 | 31.9 | 43.4 | 4.5 (*) |
| per-row `200` | 17 | 65.9 | 81.7 | 26.1 |
| | 25 | 70.7 | 40.6 | 26.2 |
| loop-invariant `200` | 17 | 89.0 | 42.2 | 26.1 |
| | 25 | 65.7 | 25.7 | 25.4 |

(*) Likely the benchmark loop vectorizing, which does not apply to per-row evaluation such as `HashPartitioning`. JDK 21 and ARM were not measured.

Harness (JMH and exhaustive equivalence check): https://gist.github.com/david-mollitor-db/1cc2fe01b478062efda9ec191efd0f51

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Results are identical for every input.

### How was this patch tested?

New cases in `ArithmeticExpressionSuite` "pmod":
- `pmod(-7, 3)` via `testNumericDataTypes`, which exercises the integral `n > 0` fast path (`Byte`/`Short` via `Int`, and `Long`);
- `pmod(-6, 3) == 0` (`Int`, `Long`): a zero remainder with a negative dividend;
- a `Long` case whose remainder is below `-2^62`, so a wrong shift count or narrowing to `Int` changes the result;
- `pmod(-1e-20, 1.0) == 0.0` (and the `Float` analogue), which needs the float/double `% n`;
- negative-divisor cases, and two assertions characterizing the pre-existing `Int`/`Long` `n < 0` wrap-around (SPARK-59934).

The integral bodies were also checked for exact equality with the released ones: all `byte` and `short` pairs, all 2^32 `int` dividends for 26 divisors (including `Int.MinValue` and `-1073741825`), and `long` edge values plus 4e8 random pairs.
